newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-WIDE RECEIVER ANDRE RISON SIGNS WITH CHIEFS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-WIDE RECEIVER ANDRE RISON SIGNS WITH CHIEFS.

text.p: Andre Rison, who restored his value around the league by filling in capably for the Super Bowl champion Green Bay Packers, signed a two-year contract with the Kansas City Chiefs Wednesday.
No financial terms of the deal were disclosed and neither year of the package is guaranteed.
The Chiefs are trying to improve their passing offence this off-season. Rison, a four-time Pro Bowl receiver, joins recently signed Brett Perriman, formerly of the Detroit Lions.

"It'a a winning organisation, a championship contender and a coach I have always respected," Rison said. "I don't want to play at any other level than a championship level and I feel this is the right place."

"Obviously, he's an experienced receiver with tremendous receiving credentials," Chiefs general manager Carl Peterson said. "He's coming off a major contribution to a Super Bowl team. He was looking for an opportunity to continue his career with a team he thinks has a legitimate chance to get to the Super Bowl."

Rison and Perriman -- along with tight end Ted Popson, who was signed Tuesday -- should provide Elvis Grbac with capable options in his first year as a full-time starter. Grbac joined Kansas City earlier in the off-season as an unrestricted free agent.
"He's a playmaking wide receiver," said Chiefs coach Marty Schottenheimer of Rison. "He makes plays and makes yardage in chunks, big chunks. He catches it and runs with it. I'm delighted."

Rison appeared in five regular-season games, catching 13 passes for 135 yards and a touchdown for the Packers. He started all three post-season games and had seven receptions for 143 yards and two scores, including a 54-yard TD that kicked off the scoring in Green Bay's 35-21 Super Bowl victory over the New England Patriots.
Rison played his rookie year of 1989 with the Indianapolis Colts before becoming one of the league's elite receivers with Atlanta from 1990-94, eclipsing 1,000 yards in four of those five years.

He then endured a frustrating season with the Cleveland Browns in 1995 and played the first 10 games of last season with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Overall, in 125 career games, Rison has 569 receptions for 7,747 yards and 66 touchdowns.
